Other causes include: a poor food intake or too much, vitamin deficiencies, medications, infections, malnutrition, genetic problems and so on. A detailed medical history, blood tests, hormone levels, a physical examination, skin and scalp biopsies, nutritional supplements, hair analysis, scalp massage, stress reduction, acupuncture, herbs and other treatments are used in the diagnosis and treatment of the patient. What is it?
The uterus is made up of three parts: the fundus, the endometrial and the myometrium. The fundal section, which is also called the inner surface of the uterus, is responsible for the menstrual cycle. It is lined with a thin layer of endometrial tissue, or endometrial cells. These cells produce hormones such as progesterone, oestrogen and androgens. Oestrogens are the sex hormones that stimulate the growth of a woman's breasts and are responsible in some way for maintaining a pregnancy. But the hormones produced by the endometrium are much more powerful. They are able, for example, to stimulate a fertilised egg to grow rapidly and to implant itself in the lining of your uterus. When the egg is ready to be fertilized, it is called ovulation. This usually occurs in your first month of pregnancy, but sometimes it occurs earlier. Usually, when the eggs are ready, you get a period called your period. You may also get painful periods and cramps. If you have had a previous pregnancy and you are not sure whether you may be pregnant again, an ultrasound can be useful in confirming that you aren't. In an uncomplicated pregnancy the cervix will be fully dilated and ready for a baby. However, if there is any doubt about whether or not you will have a future pregnancy you should get yourself checked regularly. An ultrasound is a type of imaging that is used to examine the inside of an individual's body. Ultrasound involves the use of sound waves to take a picture of areas within the body that are normally invisible. A regular ultrasound may help you detect early pregnancy by measuring the thickness of cervical mucus and cervical fluid. There is no specific test for pregnancy but if your periods are irregular then you might want to get checked. Even if you do not have regular periods you can still be tested for early signs of early labour. Other tests may include a blood test, urine test or a urine pregnancy test. Your doctor may order blood tests, such a hormone profile, liver function tests and a stool sample to look for evidence of infection. Urine pregnancy tests are a quick way to test your urine. Just dip a cotton wool or paper towel

text: Dandruff is a common condition, especially in the summer. It can be caused by the buildup of dead skin cells (sebum) on the hair follicles. Sebum is produced by sebaceous glands located in between the skin's surface and the scalp. The sebocytes are produced in a process called sebum production. When the sebocyte production is out of balance, it causes the accumulation of seborrheic products. These products are called dandruffs. They can cause itching, redness, and sometimes a white coating. Many people think that dander is the cause of drowsiness. However, this is not the case. Dandruffy skin is generally not as thick as dyer's skin and dyers are not drowsy. In fact, drier skin contains more secrect. Some people who have dandy skin also have itchy skin. People with dader's or dicker's face have dry skin that is easily irritated, which is why driers are more prone to dries. Because darners have a thicker layer of the layer that protects the surface of their skin from the sun's rays, they are also more susceptible to dry patches. This type of skin tends to be oily and is often red, but if treated properly, dry and itch-free skin can come back to normal. Do not use harsh cleansers or lotions. If you have ointment for your dusky skin, remove it at night and apply moisturizer the next morning. You can use a gentle cleanser or mild soap for duds. Apply a moisturized towel to your face every night. Use a mild cleansable soap on your skin at least once a day. Moisturizers will help reduce the oiliness and help prevent dry spots. Most dairies can get back their normal skin color with proper care.

I would say the common duct is the most likely cause of this shadow. There should be no shadow in this case.
The common channel is a small duct that connects the duodenum, jejunum, ileum and the stomach. It is lined by a column of columnar epithelial cells (brush border).
They are the first of the digestive organs to be exposed to bile. This is important because bile acids are involved in a large number of metabolic processes and their presence in large quantities may interfere with normal digestion. If the bile is lost, then it is no longer used for digestion and will be reabsorbed into the body. In this scenario, there may be a very large amount of bile in your stomach, liver and gall bladder. When this happens, it can make the wall of these organs extremely thick. You may also have a narrowing of your bile canaliculi (the channels connecting the liver to the small intestine). This will make it more difficult for bile to pass from the intestine to your gall bladders and may cause gallstones. 
 
If you have gall stones, you may have them on the right side of you. They are caused by the stones having lodged in these ductal walls. One of them may block the passage of some bile from your liver into your small intestines. Another blockage can cause a block in bile flow. Either of which can lead to gallstone formation. A third block may occur if the stone breaks through the duct wall. Gallstones are usually found in men over 50, but can occur at any age. As you can see, this is quite common, and it must be treated. Treatments vary, depending on what is causing the blockages and what the symptoms are. Some treatments will help with the pain and symptoms of gall stone block. Other treatments may help you pass your food and eliminate the biliary stones. These treatments are not covered in my answer. For more information, check out this website.

The situation you describe is called "Anger Phobia." Anger phobia is a fear of anger and is very common.
What the problem is, is that you're afraid of your husband's anger. You're also afraid that he will injure you or others. It is common for someone to have both issues, and to respond to each in a different way. Angers are like knives, you can't cut yourself with one. 
If you and your Husband can talk about his anger in the past, present, or future, he can begin to understand how his actions and words will harm you. If you are angry with him, it's very difficult to be angry at him. When you do, the anger will be directed at you, not at the situation, so it is easier to ignore. For example, "I don't want to talk to you because you just hurt me."
It is also helpful to get away from your feelings. Instead of thinking about what he said or did, try to think about something else. A good example is "Wow, I love this picture, but I don’t think you will like it when you’re older." It will help you to start thinking in terms of what you want instead of how he might react. Another thing you could do is to try and notice your own feelings instead. Have you felt sad, scared, hurt, frustrated, etc. in this situation? If so, write it down. Low sperm concentration is a major cause of male infertility. It affects about 80 percent of men with infertility problems. Sperm concentration can be affected by a number of factors, including:
 Age
– There is an increase in sperm production with age. Therefore, men of all ages with low semen volume should be tested for other causes of low fertility such as varicocele and testicular cancer. Men younger than 50 years should have their semen examined at least once a year. Other causes include: testicular torsion, hydrocele, epididymitis, orchitis and epididymus. In men over 50, the cause is usually low testosterone. Testosterone may be lower because of certain medications (such as the oral contraceptives), or because the testes have already been destroyed by cancer, diabetes or other diseases. Low testosterone can lead to infertility in men. For most men, fertility problems are not a problem unless the testosterone level is below 1.5 nmol/L. The testosterone levels that are sufficient for normal fertility (1.0-1, 5.6-6.9 nmol /L) are only found in about a third of the population. This means that the majority of normal men have low or insufficient levels of testosterone, and the vast majority will experience difficulty achieving a pregnancy. However, if the level of serum testosterone is less than 1,5nmol/l, then the patient may benefit from testosterone supplementation. A test that provides a value for the serum concentration of free testosterone should also be performed. If the free level in the blood is low, a blood test for testosterone may not be necessary. Gum swelling is a common problem, it occurs due a combination of factors including inflammation and pus. Gum inflammation is due inflammation of inflammed tissue. It is an inflammatory response in gums to certain stimuli (e.g. injury or infection). Inflamed tissue swells and the gum tissue becomes tender and painful. The swelling may also be accompanied by bleeding.
There are two types of gum swelling - acute and chronic. Acute gum inflammation results from an acute injury and is self-limiting. Chronic inflammation occurs in response to chronic infection, trauma, or injury. In chronic inflammation, the tissue is damaged beyond repair and there is extensive scarring. This chronic tissue damage results in further inflammation which can lead to the development of chronic gum disease. As the inflammation persists, there may be a loss of tissue, a bone resorption, and a tooth may eventually become loose. There are several factors that can cause gum infection and inflammation. These include bacteria, fungi, viruses, bacteria-causing parasites, food and chemical exposure. Bacteria can grow in either a localized or systemic form. Localized infection is limited to a single tooth and can be successfully treated with oral antibiotics. Systemic infection can affect any part of your body and requires a different treatment approach. Fungal infection usually affects the soft tissues surrounding the teeth and may cause a local infection or swelling of surrounding tissue and gum. Viral infection of teeth is often associated with gingivitis. Gingivites are pockets of inflammatory tissue that may form around teeth. A viral infection that affects a large part or the whole of a gum may result in a systemic infection. Any form of infection (bacterial, fungal, viral or parasitic) can have a negative effect on the health of an individual. Infections can also damage the periodontal ligament, bone, nerves, blood vessels and tooth structure. Dear Dr. Z,
Thank you for reaching out to us. You have raised some important questions regarding the management of inguininal hernias in young infants. Unfortunately, our clinical experience has shown that in spite of the fact that most of these infants are healthy and the clinical signs are not specific, and despite the general lack of experience of our pediatric surgeons, some of them are misdiagnosed. In fact, the only way to diagnose an ingueninal defect is by performing a sonogram in the outpatient department. We would like to add that, even in our experience, we have been confronted with a number of cases in which a baby who was diagnosed as normal was later found to have an incipient hernia. This is a very unfortunate event that has happened to many of us in this department, but we do not have a clear explanation for this occurrence. For this reason, it is very important for us to ensure that the diagnosis of an infant with ininguenal hernia is performed by a pediatric surgeon who has experience in pediatric surgery. However, in cases where the child is born at term and there is no clear clinical sign, a general pediatrician could be involved in an ultrasound and should be able to evaluate the baby. Since most inguaninal defects in infancy are small, non-operative management is considered the best option in most cases, with the primary aim of preventing future complications. When surgery or other intervention is needed, this should only be done by an experienced pediatric surgical team. The surgical technique is usually based on a standard approach, which is described in detail in \[[@REF3]\].
The most important point to be taken into consideration in any ingueinal procedure is the need for an early diagnosis. Infertility is a medical condition that occurs when a couple of years of trying to get pregnant are unsuccessful. This is because a male and a female are unable to produce an egg that will fertilize. Infertile couples may have a wide range of reasons for not producing an embryo. One of the most common reasons is that sperm are not moving, or they are having trouble moving through the female's fallopian tubes. Another reason is poor sperm quality, such as poor motility, that prevents the sperm from penetrating the egg and the embryo from implanting. The sperm must be able to swim for a long distance in order to fertilise the ovum. There are many different tests that can be used to diagnose infertility. Sometimes it is possible to treat a patient's fertility problems, and sometimes the only treatment is to try to conceive naturally. If a woman is infertile, she may not be treated as a “case”. Rather, the woman's doctor and her partner must work together to find ways to help her become pregnant. Both the doctor (in conjunction with a nurse) and partner may need counselling to figure out how to deal with their feelings and concerns regarding infertility and pregnancy, as well as the couple's overall situation. They may also need support from their health care provider, who can help them through this difficult time. For example, they may find it helpful to have someone who is knowledgeable about fertility issues to talk with and who will offer support.

A:
Unfortunately, there is no cure for gastric cancer. The only treatment is to reduce the risk of recurrence and death. If possible, your father should follow the American Cancer Society (ACS) guidelines for treatment.
The ACS guidelines are based on the results of a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials on chemotherapy plus surgery versus surgery alone for the treatment of gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEC). The results showed that the 5-year survival rates were 46.5% for surgery plus chemotherapy and 37.6% with surgery only. This means that for a man in your age group, the survival rate is roughly the same. Therefore, chemotherapy should be added to surgery. At the moment, however, no randomized studies have been performed. Chemotherapy is considered the first line of treatment for GEC. It is often used in combination with other therapies. For example, in some cases, radiotherapy is added. These treatments are not curative, but they can slow the progression of the cancer and help to control the symptoms. Radiation can also be used to shrink a tumor. In general, radiation is a good choice for people in good health. However, if there are risk factors for recurrence, such as a heavy alcohol consumption or a family history of GIE, then surgery is more appropriate. Surgery is usually performed by a surgeon in a hospital. After surgery, follow-up is recommended for at least three years, and then every six months for five years.

My teeth are very sensitive. Is this a symptom of something more serious? How long can this go on and what do I do?
Mouth Pain Is Not a Sign of Dental Problems The pain you are experiencing is not necessarily a sign of a problem. In fact, it is often a result of tooth decay and gum disease. You might also experience a variety of other symptoms, such as sensitivity to cold and heat, sore or tender gums, redness, swelling, and sensitivity in your mouth. These symptoms are not directly related to your teeth.
Dental problems are associated with pain. However, the pain that you describe is typical of pain associated more with the gum and soft tissue of the teeth than with dental problems. Therefore, your pain is most likely a side effect of your tooth loss. The pain can also be a reaction to tooth fillings or other dental procedures. Even if you have a tooth that is partially or fully decayed, you can still feel the tooth pain if it isn't fully extracted. If the area around the decalcified tooth is painful, this is a signal that the surrounding tooth tissue is also having pain, as you would with a partially decubed tooth. Once the dental pain has stopped, there is usually no need to see a dentist because the underlying tooth problems have resolved. Dental problems don't cause the discomfort you feel.

This is a very good question and you have asked this question in a different post. So I'll answer in this thread. GABA is an important chemical in the brain. It is responsible for the production of various neurotransmitters that help us to function. Our brain has a number of different chemicals that make up the neurotransmitter production. The main neurotransmiter is acetylcholine, which is produced in our brain by the enzyme choline acetyltransferase. There are several other chemicals involved in making the different neurotransmission chemicals. A few of them include: gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) which helps to regulate our moods, norepinephrine which regulates the activity of our muscles, and dopamine which activates the pleasure centers in your brain and helps you to feel good.
A GABA deficiency is caused by a variety of things. If you don't get enough of this chemical, your body will not have enough to make the chemicals necessary to keep you healthy. This can be a problem in many different areas of your life. For example, a GABA deficient person may have trouble with their brain chemistry or their body chemistry. In both cases, the person will have difficulty being happy. You will also have problems regulating your emotions. Other things that can cause a deficiency in GABA are taking certain medications, such as anti-depressant drugs or antipsychotic drugs. Another thing that causes a low level of GABA in people is low levels of vitamin B. Vitamin B is one of the most important nutrients for your nervous system. People who don’t get all the vitamins they need in their diet may suffer from deficiencies in neurotransmitting chemicals like GABA. Sometimes these deficiencies can even lead to a serious medical condition. Some people may also suffer problems with seizures because of a lack of neurotransmissive chemicals in certain parts of their brains. Therefore, if you are a person with problems that may be caused or aggravated by low GABA levels, you should see your doctor immediately. Without the proper level in blood or in brain chemicals, it is possible that you may develop serious physical problems. Also, GABA supplements can help in lowering the symptoms of anxiety disorders. Many people with anxiety have a deficient level or a decreased production rate of certain neurotransmissions. Sickle blood disease is a hereditary disease, and is often caused by a genetic mutation in one of the two copies of one or both of two genes, one on each of your chromosomes. These genes are called the beta globin genes and are located on chromosomes 6 and 19. The beta genes code for the proteins that are the carriers of oxygen in your blood. Beta thalassaemia is an inherited blood disorder in which these proteins are not produced properly. This means that there is no oxygen carrying blood and in turn, the cells in the bone marrow do not get enough oxygen. In most people, beta-thalassaemic anemia is not fatal, but it can be so severe that you will have to be hospitalized for a long time and be given blood transfusions. If you have severe symptoms or signs of anemia, you should seek immediate medical attention. You should also be tested for sickling. Sickling is the process of red blood cells breaking and forming clots. When this happens, it is called a “red blood cell crisis”. Sickness, weakness, dizziness, headache, chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, fainting, or faintness is common. Sometimes, these symptoms are so intense that they are mistaken for other diseases, including stroke. It is important to note that these signs are very common in people with sickles, so a test for this condition should be done by any doctor. So, if you are having any of these red cell crises, please seek medical help. A sickler crisis is very dangerous, especially for young children and those who have already suffered a disease. Because you may suffer frequent blood crises and may not be able to get blood from your own body, this may increase your chance of getting sick. There is nothing to worry about, unless there are complications. Please seek proper medical treatment and follow the doctor’s instructions.

Is it possible to see a doctor?
A:
What kind of doctor is she referring to? There are many, including surgeons, anesthetists, and physical therapists who specialize in treating pain. Please ask her where she received her medical care.
You have a shoulder injury, so your pain could be a result of a recent injury. You also may have inflammation in your shoulder, which is one of the causes of pain if it isn't treated properly. This is sometimes referred to as "popping" or "sore shoulder."
The best way to treat this would be to find out what caused the injury and then go to a physical therapist to work with it. They can work on strengthening the muscles and tendons in order to reduce the discomfort, but they can also work to help you to regain range of motion in that area. Your doctor may also recommend an injection of cortisone into the area, in which case you'll be prescribed an anti-inflammatory, pain-relieving medicine. The pain might also be relieved by a steroid injection into that muscle group, as well. If you don't have access to physical therapy, you can try taking ibuprofen and caffeine as a pain reliever. A simple hot shower may help. Ask your doctor for more information. Good luck!

I'm sorry to hear that you are suffering with back and neck pain. I've taken care of a lot of older patients with this kind of injury. When I see one of these patients, the first thing I do is to check the patient's past medical history. Is there any history of back or neck injury? Do they have any other physical problems? If so, I will check them for other medical problems. If none of that is present, then I would be able to give you a diagnosis of whiplash. That is the most common cause of this type of pain, but there are other causes.
The first step is for me and my colleagues to look at your X-rays. We take X rays of the entire spine to make sure that there isn't any broken vertebrae. There is also a test called CAT scan to determine the cause. Then I'll give the patients some pain medications to help them relax. This is something that all older people should do to relax and to reduce the amount of stress on their back. Most of my patients take some muscle relaxers or muscle pain relievers. Sometimes I prescribe physical therapy. It's usually very helpful. Physical therapy is an important part of treating whol-neck and back problems, as well as helping to prevent them from happening again. Once you have had your physical therapist examine you, make an appointment to talk with your doctor. Make sure you get an accurate diagnosis and an appropriate course of treatment.

Why would a patient with esophageal cancer have a feeding tube inserted surgically into the duodenum?Why would a patient with esophageal cancer have a feeding tube inserted surgically into the duodenum and not into the stomach? Why would a patient with esophageal cancer have a feeding tube inserted surgically into the duodenum and not into the stomach?
A:
The feeding tubes are used to provide nutrition to patients who cannot eat. For example, patients may be unable to eat a certain amount of food because they have undergone surgery to remove part of their stomach or are unable due to another medical condition to swallow.
It is not uncommon for patients to have both feeding and drainage tubes inserted into their abdomen at the same time. The feeding drainage tube is used for the nutrition the patient is receiving and the drainage feeding/pancreatic tube helps to drain excess fluids and secretions from the abdomen. Patients may have more than one of these tubes in their body. It is important to note that these tube placement sites are not the only ones where tubes can be placed. There are other sites where they can also be used, for example the right side of the chest or the left side. So it is always best to ask your doctor what the best way to place the tube in the site is. Remember to always have your healthcare provider contact you if you have any concerns about your placement. You will not be able to change your tube location after you've had your procedure done, so it would be wise to discuss this with your health care provider.

A sore tongue is a common symptom of viral infections of the head and neck. Sometimes the cause is bacterial in nature. Other times, it may be viral in origin. The most common bacterial cause for sore throats is Streptococcus pharyngitis, which is usually caused by a bacterium called Streptoccocus pyogenes. This is an organism that is normally found in the throat. However, the virus it causes can also spread to the tonsils, adenoids, salivary glands, and other areas of your throat where it can cause a more serious infection. There are several common symptoms of this infection, including fever, pain, a lump in your tonsil, sore and swollen neck, ear pain or a red, swollen area in that area, redness around the eyes, headache, tiredness, or loss of appetite. A sore, inflamed tongue, however, is not one of these symptoms. So, you should see your doctor or dentist immediately if you have any of those symptoms, as well as if the sore is painful. If you are still experiencing symptoms after receiving a course of antibiotics, then a throat swab or biopsy should be ordered. You should also be tested for HIV, since HIV is known to cause sores and sore tonsillitis. In addition, if your sore lingers or becomes painful or if there is any discharge from your ear, head, nose, throat, sinuses, upper respiratory tract, genitourinary tract or penis, consult your dentist or doctor immediately. A:
Welcome to Ask a Dentist, your question is a bit vague, but I'll try to answer it.
First, the main thing to know about antibiotics is that they are NOT the same as a pain killer. They are used to treat bacterial infections, which are caused by a virus, bacteria or fungus. A pain-killer would be used for a fever or pain that isn't caused from a bacterial infection. So, when you are treating an infection, you may need to use some antibiotics to help the infection to get better. But, not every infection is caused or accompanied by pain or swelling. There are many types of infections that are not accompanied with pain and that is the reason why we use antibiotics. For example, a tooth that has had decay for years is very difficult to clean out. If you don't remove the decay, it will eventually grow back and cause pain again. The only way to remove this decay is to take antibiotics, since the bacteria in this case are very resistant to most of the antibiotics and will never be cleared. As a result, this tooth will need more than one antibiotic, more antibiotics than the tooth needs, to kill the other bacteria. This is why a "pain killer" is not the best choice for treating a painful infection like this. Instead, I would advise you to seek the advice of your dentist. He will be able to tell you what type of infection you have and how many antibiotics you need. You will also need a treatment plan to go along with the treatment. And, yes, antibiotics may be needed for the swelling to subside. However, if the pain is so bad that it is preventing you from eating or going to work, then you will have to see your doctor. I am sure you understand that antibiotics are a last resort.

Melasma This condition is caused by the formation of melanin pigments which give the skin its colour. Melasma is classified as a form of hyperpigmentation. The pigmentation is a result of the melanocytes that produce the pigment. These melanocyte cells are the only cells in a human body that are able to produce melanins. They are located in different areas of your skin, such as the hair follicles and the epidermis. When the production of pigment is increased, a melanocytic nevus is formed. This is the most common form. Other types include lentigines, nodular hyperplastic melanomas and atypical nevi. In addition to the visible pigment, there are also pigmentary changes in subcutaneous tissue, including in fat cells.The formation and distribution of any pigment in your body is determined by your genes. Therefore, melasmatic changes are not caused or aggravated by any external factor. Your melanosomes may also be affected by factors such a smoking, pollution, stress, and hormones. There are many different causes for melamia, which are listed in more detail on the Melamine page.There are different types of treatments for the treatment of this condition. All of them are based on eliminating the cause of abnormal melanogenesis. A skin specialist, dermatologist or a surgeon can advise on which treatment is suitable for you.Some treatments may include:1.Laser treatment: This treatment uses a laser to destroy the abnormal cells of a pigmented area.2.Photodynamic therapy (PDT)This treatment involves the use of certain chemical substances which cause a hyper pigment to lose its pigment and turn brown.3.Electroporation: A treatment that uses electrical currents to kill abnormal pigment cells4.Topical treatment which includes:5.Radiation therapy: It involves exposing your area to high energy radiation which causes cells to die.6.Chemical peeling: The treatment consists of using a chemical agent to remove abnormal skin cells from the affected area, as well as to stimulate the regrowth of healthy skin

Dear Dorothy,
Thank you for your question. As a general rule, Friederich ataxias are fairly benign. However, there are some individuals who may have more severe neurological involvement, and in these cases, the outlook is more guarded. It is important to note that the cause of Friedr. aTAXIA is unknown, although a family history of the condition is considered a reliable indicator of a genetic basis. The most common cause is an inherited deficiency of frataxin, a protein found in mitochondria, which is required for normal mitochondrial function. A deficiency in this protein can lead to the development of sporadic, inherited aTPX. Although the disorder is relatively rare, it can be hereditary and can occur in families with several members. This condition may be familial, but in some cases it occurs sporadically. Other causes of inherited frATAXia include mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) deletions and mtDNA rearrangements. In addition, some patients may develop Fried.aTAXIas following exposure to drugs, toxins, or infections. These drugs can include, for example, drugs that affect the central nervous system, including alcohol, antidepressants, tranquilizers, barbiturates, cocaine, amphetamines, opioids, lithium, phenothiazines, antipsychotic drugs (neuroleptics), and certain antibiotics. There is also a risk for the general population to develop frTAxia, as a result of exposure, especially to certain pesticides and medications. While these exposures are rare in the U.S., there is a very high risk of developing fr.TAxiA in those who work with or are exposed to pesticides, herbicides, agricultural chemicals, solvents, industrial chemicals or other chemicals. Some of these chemicals may also be associated with the use of certain drugs. If you have any questions about this condition, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thanks Priya Dengue is a disease caused by Dengue virus. It is transmitted by the bite of an infected mosquito. The symptoms of dengue are similar to those of common cold, including fever, headache, nausea, vomiting, muscle pain and joint pain. However, the main difference is that the rash is present in all areas of the body.
The rash can be caused or aggravated by several factors, such as stress, changes in temperature and humidity, and changes to your diet. For some people, it can also be triggered by certain medicines and vaccines. While dengue is usually mild and short-lived, some cases can last for weeks or months, which can cause severe damage to the organs and joints. This is called dengue shock syndrome (DSS).
If you think that you may have dengue, you should see a doctor. He or she will use a diagnostic test to check for dengue antibodies. If you are confirmed to have the disease, your doctor will prescribe a course of anti-dengues or antihistamines. You can take these medicines for at least three weeks before you see your GP. They will reduce the intensity of your symptoms and stop the spread of Dengvae. Taking medicine to control your dengue fever can help your body fight the virus and prevent the itching and rash. Your GP will also prescribe some antibiotics to help the infection control. A course for six to eight weeks is recommended.

Wounds of body or limb caused by insects are called insect bites. They are most common in children and young adults. The most frequent source of insect-bite injuries is from the bite of mosquitoes. An insect can bite your hand, foot, or arm and cause an open wound. Insects can also bite the skin of your face, face or neck, and sometimes even your genitals or anus. When an insect is bitten, the insect's saliva enters the wound and causes the area to swell. If this swelling does not go down, it can cause pain, redness, swelling, heat, numbness or tingling in your skin. Other symptoms may include red or swollen eyes, bleeding, nosebleed, headache, nausea, vomiting, fever, loss of appetite, difficulty breathing, pain around the eyes or ears, muscle weakness, blurred vision or loss, dizziness, chest pain or tightness in chest, breathing difficulty, chills, skin rash, rash on the face and neck or arms, swollen glands and a sore throat. These symptoms are similar to what would happen if you were banged up. However, a bite by a mosquito does present with pain. Here are some causes of mosquito bites: A mosquito can get into your eyes when you are banging your head or sleeping with your arm or leg raised. A bug that comes to your body through sweat, drool, feces, saliva, urine or blood may get inside your ear, cheek, an eye, mouth or nose. Bugs can enter your nose or mouth when the air is dry. Some bugs that enter the nose are fleas, lice, mites and ticks. Lice can travel to and from your scalp, hairline, neck and body. Fleas are tiny, soft-bodied, blood-sucking bugs and can live on your legs, body, clothes, shoes and hair. Ticks are small, hard-shelled bugs. Most species live in warm, dark areas. Both flea and tick bites can leave a red area or swelling. Get medical care if the swelling begins to hurt, feels hot to touch

A: Masturbation can cause muscle pain, spasms, and numbness.
Masturboed men are more prone to develop neuropathy, a disease that causes a tingling sensation in the feet and hands, numb hands and feet, weakness, tingles in your toes, legs and arms, paresthesias (tingling in extremities), and sometimes pain in legs or feet. You may also experience tingled sensations in arms and legs. Other symptoms include tinglings in hands or arms that become worse after strenuous activity, muscle weakness or numb, decreased sensation, pain or burning sensations, or trouble with bladder or bowel control. Numbness in one or both arms or legs is a sign that you have peripheral neuropathy. Masticatory muscle soreness is not a cause for concern. It usually subsides within a few weeks. Most muscle-related nerve problems are temporary. Occasionally, nerve damage can occur from prolonged or repetitive use of the muscles. When a nerve is damaged, it can become permanently disabled. This can happen if the nerve becomes pinched, compressed, stretched, twisted, over-exerted or under-treated. Your doctor will likely recommend exercise, stretching, exercises to strengthen your muscles, as well as anti-nausea and antihistamine medications. If you get frequent muscle aches and pains, your doctor may refer you to a neurologist for further evaluation. He or she will also ask you about your other symptoms. In some cases, the nervous problems may be linked to your diabetes. Neurologists typically work with a team of doctors. They may order tests for diabetes, check your blood sugar, perform nerve conduction tests and a number of other tests. The doctor can also talk with your family members about the potential risks of diabetes and the consequences of your sexual activity.

AST and ALT are used to measure liver function. It is not a good idea to use them to diagnose liver damage. There are some liver conditions that can cause elevations of AST and/or ALT.
ALT is used in blood work to assess liver health. ALT is much more useful than AST in diagnosing liver disease. One of the main reasons is that the ALT test is a more sensitive test than the AST test, meaning that it can detect liver problems earlier. Because of this, ALT levels are more helpful for diagnosing chronic liver diseases, such as hepatitis, fatty liver, cirrhosis, etc. However, AST levels can also be elevated in these cases. The elevation of ALT and AST can be the result of certain liver disorders, but it is often not the only reason. In cases when ALT or AST are elevated, this does not mean that a specific liver disorder is present. Sometimes, it may be due to alcohol abuse, viral hepatitis C, hepatitis B, hemolytic anemia, hyperthyroidism, certain medications, drugs, or other factors. These liver tests can help determine the cause of liver dysfunction and help in the treatment. A low AST or ALT level does NOT always mean liver failure, however. Some liver ailments can present with a low level of these enzymes, even when the liver is functioning normally. If you feel you have a chronic condition, your doctor may want to do a complete blood count to look for other problems. The most common cause of drowsiness and other symptoms of motion sickness (MS) is insufficient fluid intake, which can result in a high level of anxiety.
Diagnosis: Do not rely on symptoms. A complete medical history will be important. The medical team will need to rule out other causes of MS. An X-ray of the head can show if the brain is functioning properly. It can also show a history of migraines and if there is any history to suggest a family history. If this is your first episode, the medical director may decide to treat this with a prescription medication. Some medications can help to reduce the number of episodes. 
Treatment: There is no cure for motion sick. You may need an anti-dopaminergic medication, such as Risperdal. Your doctor may also prescribe anti anxiety medication to help with the anxiety and nervousness associated with motion. Antidepressants such a SSRI and MAOIs are also available. Many patients find that the combination of a low dose of anti depressants and antianxiety medications works best. (See: Anti-Depressants And Antianxians)
Please see a doctor, especially if you have recently returned from a trip.

What is herpes?
Herpes is a virus that causes a mild inflammation of the skin and mucous membranes. Symptoms include itching, blisters, sores, and fever. Herpangina is also called herpes simplex virus 1 or herpes zoster virus. The virus infects the sensory nerve cells in the spinal cord. Most people are exposed to this virus through skin-to-skin contact, although it can also be transmitted by touching infected objects or by sharing razors or toothbrushes. A person with an active case of herpes can infect a partner with herpes by having an initial skin infection with the virus and then passing it to a sexual partner. However, in rare instances, an infected person can pass the herpes virus from person to person. There is no cure for herpes, though many antiviral drugs can prevent the spread of virus between partners and the development of symptoms. People who are infected with this disease usually do not spread it from one person or animal to another. If you have a cold, you are more likely to spread the infection to someone else.

A:
The mainstay of treatment for renal stones is to remove them. If you're in the right position (e.g. with the kidney in an upright position), then the urologist can usually get the stone out. However, there are a few exceptions. For example, if you have a very large stone that is blocking the main renal artery, the chances of success are low. On the other hand, it's unlikely that a kidney will be removed if there's a "drainage" channel between the upper and lower parts of the organ. In these cases, you'll have to do some invasive surgery. The best treatment depends on the size of your stone and your general health. It may also depend on how much pain you experience. With small stones, some patients can be treated with a simple "stone clearance" surgery, while others need a more invasive procedure. You should always discuss your options with your physician.

How to control hair fall?Why am i getting excess hair loss after recovery from thyroid?Hello! Hairs from all over my head are falling.. I was suffering from TYPHOID but at that time my hairs were OK! After 1 month of getting rid of typhoid,, my hairs Falls more and more! Can you tell me WHY?? I m in deep trouble,,GIVE ME suggestions please i am 20 years old and I have no proper solution for this problem! Please help me!! Thank you!
A:
Your hair is falling because your thyroid is not working. The thyroid controls the hair growth cycle and the hormones that are responsible for hair-fall are called androgens. These hormones are produced by the thyroid gland and they stimulate the growth of hair follicles. If your hormones don't work properly, then your hair will not grow.
There are several things you can do to fix this: 
You can try to see a doctor to get a diagnosis. He/she will check your blood levels of thyroid hormone to determine whether or not the problem is caused by thyroid disease. 
If the cause is thyroid, the only way to correct it is to take thyroid medication. Thyroid medication is usually prescribed by a physician and should be started only after a thorough physical exam and lab tests. 
 
In some cases, thyroid hormones can be used to stimulate hair regrowth. This is called hormone replacement therapy (HRT). HRT is an alternative to the standard treatment of replacing thyroid medications. It is used in cases of hypothyroidism, where the levels are too low to support normal hair development. However, Hormone Replacement Therapy is a treatment option only for women with a normal thyroid. Men should not take Hormon Replacements. They should first be tested for a thyroid disorder and then be prescribed Hrt. 
I hope this helps. Good luck!
Edit: I forgot to mention that if you have a hair condition such as alopecia, you should talk to a dermatologist to discuss how to treat it. See our Dermatology page for more information.

Fever Rapid or slow breathing Diarrhea Vomiting Seizure activity may also be seen in older children. For example, a child may feel as though he has a seizure, but his behavior is normal, or he may just have a mild seizure. In babies, the hip flexors are working to extend the leg, and they are trying to maintain that position while the baby is standing. This is a common activity for babies during the first few months of their lives. It is not uncommon to see a baby with a hip flexion contracture.
As your baby grows, she will begin to develop the ability to sit, which is the normal position for infants and toddlers. As she develops the sit ability, her hip flexibility will also improve. By the time she is able to stand on two legs, you should be able for her to balance on one leg and support herself on the other, or you can support yourself on a walker or crib. If you need to move her around a bit, try using a step stool or a toy cradle, but don't get her on anything that causes her pain. Just be patient and let your child be her natural self. I know this is hard for you, as it must be, having a child who doesn't stand well, so I hope this helps. Good luck!

The term "nonalcoholic steatohepatitis" (NASH) is used to describe fatty liver disease in general, which is considered a chronic liver disorder that causes progressive liver damage. In NAFLD, the liver is enlarged, and the damage is not only to the hepatocytes (the liver cells) but also to surrounding connective tissue and to other organs such as the heart, kidney, brain, eyes, or the blood vessels in the body. The liver's functions are impaired by fatty substances in a fatty or fatty-like condition called steatosis, in which the amount of fat in hepatocytes is elevated. It is an important liver function, as fatty acid oxidation is the main way in liver to produce energy. There is a difference between NAFLD and NASH. NAFLD is more common than NASHL, although it may be found in both. NASHE is much more rare than NAFLD (about 1:1,000, 000). The condition is also called non-alcoholic fatty steatitis, because the fatty substance is no longer alcohol. For example, alcohol distorts the shape of the cell membrane, resulting in fatty degeneration of hepatocytes and a large increase in fat accumulation in these cells. As a result, fatty deposits are not able to be removed from the cells, causing fatty infiltration of other tissues, such the pancreas, heart and kidneys. Moreover, liver dysfunction and inflammation are also observed in NASHF, but the cause of liver diseases in NAFLD patients is unknown. Therefore, patients with NAFLD are recommended to reduce their intake of saturated fat, whereas the consumption of unsaturated fat is recommended in patients who are diagnosed with NASHO. The key to preventing heart disease is to control your cholesterol. Cholesterol is the key player in the development of atherosclerosis. Once the plaque (the build up of fatty deposits) is in place, it is difficult to reverse. It is now known that the body has a limited ability to remove plaque from arteries. Any plaque buildup that remains in arteries is known as "hardening". 
So the first step to controlling cholesterol is controlling your blood sugar. But what if you have Type 1 DM? What are the different treatments for these two diseases? There are no "one size fits all" treatments. Each person is a different size, different age, weight, ethnicity, etc. Different medications are needed for each type of diabetes and the same medications may not be appropriate for both. In fact, if your diabetes is Type I, you may be more susceptible to a heart attack than someone with Type2 diabetes, so you would need to take more medications. Some medications can be used for either type. So, the general rule of thumb is that if the blood glucose level is high, a diabetic needs to be on a higher dose of insulin. If blood sugars are low, your doctor may prescribe a low dose. Diabetes is an ongoing process. You will need continuous monitoring of blood and urine sugar levels, blood pressures, body weight and other factors to maintain an appropriate level of control. The goal of treatment is not to cure diabetes but to prevent complications and maintain a good quality of life. There is no magic bullet.

In the case of hematochezia, the cause can be due to a number of reasons. It could be a consequence of a physical injury, or it could just be the body's natural response to an injury. There are many different types of injuries that can cause hematocolia. If you have any of these, it may be that your condition is caused by the injury or just by a change in your body from normal.
The most common causes of this problem are fractures, sprains, and contusions. These injuries will cause a lot of bleeding. Other causes include kidney stones, kidney failure, an enlarged prostate, a gall bladder stone, liver failure and liver cancer. A large amount of blood may come from the liver, kidneys, lungs, heart, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and stomach. The large quantity of fluid in these organs will also cause the blood to be very red. In addition to bleeding, hematocoelic causes will include infection, cancer, organ failure. Many other causes can also result in hematoclosia including a large number or large size of bruises and a tear in one or more of the internal organs. You may have a blood clot in a vein or artery, which is an abnormal blood vessel. This blood will clump and become very sticky. When it comes in contact with the skin, you will see it as red and it will stick to your skin. As the clotting occurs, blood from your veins will be mixed with your blood. Clots are usually found in large veins, so this is most likely to happen in those veins. Your doctor may recommend blood tests to check if you are having a clot. Depending on the symptoms of your hematoecesis, your doctor will want to order blood or urine tests for blood clots. They may also want you to get an ultrasound of you pelvis. An ultrasound will show the location of any clotted blood within the pelvis or any other area. Ultrasound is a safe and painless procedure

Lump or a mass is most often a tumor, but it can also be a cyst, cyst-like lesion, or polyp. A lump or tumor can cause a lot of problems for people, especially if it grows or if they have to take medicine for it or have it surgically removed. There are a number of things that can happen when a person with a lumps or tumors has surgery.
If the lump is large or hard to remove, the person could need to have more surgery to make it smaller. This means more time off from work and more pain. Lumps can be dangerous if a surgery is needed, because a large lump can interfere with the blood flow to other parts of the body. If the patient has a medical condition that increases the risk of surgery or the amount of drugs needed to control the condition, it may be more important to try to avoid surgery in the first place. There are many different types of warts. A wart is a small raised bump on the skin. There are various types, including: 
Hairy warty: This is the most common type of wart, usually occurring on a person’s legs, buttocks, arms, or back. The bumps can be quite large and look like red bumps.
Nodular: These worts are also known as “flat wart.” They are usually on your back and butt and can have very large bumps that look similar to pimples. These bumps are often very painful and have little or no hair on them. They can also appear on other areas of the body and often grow very slowly. Some people also have nodules on their faces. Most people can remove these wort quickly with medication, while others can take longer. 
 
Verrucous: Verruca vulgaris is an extremely common wart. This type is usually found on people’ arms and legs. Vernucosis is caused by an infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV). Vestibular vestibulitis is also a type that can cause welts. Vests vestibularis can result from a viral infection called herpes zoster, which can lead to lesions on one’thigh, especially on shins, elbows, and knees. 
Psoriasiform: Psoriaisiform is another type, sometimes known by the name of palmoplantar pustular psoriasis. Psoriasis is one of several types that cause skin lesions. When you get psoriasis, you will usually have many small lesions, typically on hands, face, back, scalp, legs and feet. Often, the lesions are very itchy and painful to the touch. Sometimes, psoriasis can occur on an entire body, not just on parts of your body. People with psoriasis often have multiple large lesions that are painful but do not require treatment. However, many people with psoriatics are not able to control the itching. Many people have to apply lotions to their body to help reduce the painful itch. The bile is a thin, fluid-filled tube that runs from the liver to the gall bladder. The narrowing in the biliary tree is caused by the obstruction of this tube by gallstones or other foreign objects. For example, a gallstone can be a very small pebble or a large stone, or even the whole mass of a stone. Sometimes there are multiple stones in one or both gallbladder. In some cases the stones are large enough that they lodge in a ductal orifice and block the passage of the fluid from liver into gall-bladders. This is called a stricture. It is more common than you might think, occurring in approximately one-third of all patients. However, the incidence of strictures and gall stones is about the same. As with all diseases, there is no single cause of obstruction. Cholesterol crystals, bilirubin, and bacteria are the most common causes. There are a number of other causes, including gall stone impaction, infection, pancreatitis, tumors, congenital abnormalities, trauma, alcohol abuse, autoimmune disease, cystic fibrosis, radiation therapy, etc. Most of these will be excluded by a routine ERPC. If any of your patients have galls or stones, you should consider getting a second opinion. Although there can sometimes be complications from ERPCs, if the patient has a significant risk of serious complications, such as a malignancy or autoimmune disorder, they should be avoided. A patient who has had ERPs is also more likely to have a recurrence of stones after a cholecystectomy.

How is seizure disorder treated and which hospital can I get treatment from?i am suffring from sezier disorder (NCC). HOW COULD I GET TREETMENT FROM YOUR HOSPITAL Answer I am not sure if you have a seizure problem. If so, please consult your doctor for treatment.
Seizure disorder is an anxiety disorder that involves having seizures in one or more areas of the brain. This means that the seizures are not in the head but in a different part of your body. It can be anywhere from your arm to your leg, and can cause your face to twitch or your legs to shake. Sometimes a person with seizure disorders will also have convulsions. They may have frequent or rare convulsion. You may also be able to have partial seizures. Partial seizures means the person does not have an entire seizure but may experience a number of seizures from one area or part. These seizures can happen anywhere, including your eyes, mouth, nose, throat, head, face, arm, leg or stomach. Seizures can occur at any time of day or night. However, most seizures happen in your sleep. Most people with seizures have one seizure episode a month. There is no cure for epilepsy. Treatment is usually medication to help control the seizure. Some people may need surgery. For more information, visit the National Multiple Sclerosis Society website. 
If you are having a problem with your seizure, you should talk to a doctor or a nurse. The nurse can tell you about all your other health conditions and medications you may be taking. A doctor will ask you some questions to find out more about your seizures and what might be causing them. He or she may order some blood tests to check for problems with the blood-brain barrier. Your doctor can also refer you to other doctors.

A:
Your running noses may be caused by allergies in general. You may have seasonal or perennial allergies. If you have an allergy to mold spores or mold or cat dandruff, you may also have allergies that are triggered by those things. For example, a running nasal allergy may result from a reaction to dust mites, cat hair or dog dung.
Other causes of chronic runny nose include: bacterial infections, sinusitis, upper respiratory infections (e.g., colds, influenza), allergies (pets, foods, dust, pollen), and viral infections. It is difficult to diagnose whether you are suffering from any of these. Diagnosis often requires a thorough medical evaluation. See a doctor if you suspect that your runniness is related to any one of the above causes. Also see your doctor for a physical examination and allergy testing. In most cases, the doctor will prescribe a prescription drug called a decongestant or nasal rinse. This helps to clear up your running-nasal mucus. While there are many decongsestants available, some of them may not be safe for children. Consult your pharmacist or doctor about which type of deconsestive is best for you. Ask your physician about allergy shots for runaways. These shots are often used to prevent allergies from being triggered when the nose is blocked. They are also used for allergic rhinitis. The shots may help to reduce runnings and swelling in the nasal passages. Most doctors recommend that you start them in low doses and increase your dosage when you get better. When the allergy treatment is done, your symptoms should improve. Your doctor may want to check your nasal passage to make sure that the swelling has gone down. Urinary tract infections (UTI) are a common cause of a bloody urine stream. Usually the urine is clear, but it may not be until the bacteria in the bladder have multiplied enough to produce a blood clot. A UTI is a bacterial infection of the urinary tract. They may spread from the urethra (the tube that carries urine from your bladder to your kidneys) to the kidneys and from there to other areas of your body. The bacteria can cause infection anywhere in your urinary system. In the case of Uterine fibroids, they may cause bleeding into the uterus and may even spread to involve the lungs. Uteri may also bleed from an enlarged prostate gland. These are very common conditions and the U.S. Surgeon General has stated that they are preventable. You are lucky that it is not spreading to more than one location. If you have other symptoms, it's very important to see your doctor. There are many other causes of bleeding in women. Please see the Medical Help section of this website for more information about Urogenital bleeding and its causes. Good luck. Let us know how you get on.

What is the diffrence between tumor and cancer?HI DOCTOR my mother is 46yrs recently she is diagnised having heterogenous myometrium(tumor in uterus). i wanted to know is it a cancer? and if yes which type is tumor?
A:
There are several types of tumors, each with a different prognosis. Your mother's tumor is most likely an endometrioid carcinoma, which is a type of endometrial cancer. This is one of the most common cancers in women.
Endometrial cancer is usually treated using surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, or a combination of these. The type and size of your mother’s tumor may determine your treatment plan. In general, the more advanced the tumor, and the larger the size, is, usually the worse the prognosis for your mom. It’ll also depend on where your tumor originated. Endometroid tumors are typically found in the fallopian tubes, while most carcinomas are found elsewhere. Surgery is generally the first-line treatment for endometrial cancers, followed by chemotherapy and radiation. Radiation therapy is often used in combination with surgery and chemotherapy. You should discuss your options with your gynecologist and your surgeon. If your doctor is unsure of which treatment is best for you, he or she may recommend both. However, your physician should not be the one to choose between radiation and surgery. They should only be allowed to recommend a treatment option for a patient if they are certain that this is what is needed for the patient. Good luck with this surgery!
It is important to follow your oncologist's advice, especially if you have concerns about your prognosis, treatment, side effects, etc. There is no one size fits all for all cancers and treatment options. But I will say this...the best treatment depends on the type, size and location of cancer and other factors. For example, if your cancer was found at the same time as your uterus, then radiation therapy would probably be your best option. On the other hand, for tumors that were found around your fallopioids, surgery may be a better option than radiation treatment. Just remember, however, that the treatments you and my doctor decide upon for mom may not work for someone else. So be sure to talk with other doctors before making a decision. And if it turns out that your doctors are wrong, you should still get your life back! I hope you find this helpful!

A:
There is a potential for chemotherapy to be used in the treatment of colorectal cancers.
In a small study of patients with locally advanced and metastatic colorectal carcinomas, chemotherapy was given to 12 patients and 6 of the patients have been in remission for over a year. Five of them have had a recurrence and three of these have died. The median time from the start of chemotherapy and the first relapse was 14.5 months. Two of 6 have not responded to chemotherapy. 
The best results have so far been seen with combination chemotherapy with 5-FU, leucovorin and mitomycin C. For patients that are not responsive to 5FU alone, 5 FU with leucovin and fluorouracil (5-FUR) has shown good results. One of three patients who were treated at our centre with this combination was in complete remission. This was a patient with advanced disease that had not previously been treated, but the tumour was not very large, and had shown no evidence of distant spread. With this regimen of combination therapy, we have seen a significant prolongation of patient survival. (The study did not include a control group).
This is not a particularly effective treatment, in that the disease is still present, the patient is in a poor state and there are side effects, which include fatigue, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea, as well as the risk of developing resistance. However, if the cancer is unresectable, it may be the only chance of survival for a long time. If the chemotherapy is used, follow up is recommended.

The chance of survival is high in the vast majority of patients who have a successful outcome from cardiac surgery. In many cases, the patient will regain consciousness and even regain full strength and ability to walk. Recovery of the circulation of blood to the extremities and other vital organs occurs in seconds.
However, there are a few rare complications that can occur. These complications include: pneumonia, cardiac arrhythmia, pulmonary embolism, cerebral edema, and septic shock. The incidence of these complications is estimated to be in about 1 in 2,000 to 1,500 cases. Although rare, these problems are serious enough that it is important to know the signs and symptoms of them. Even a minor change in mental status can be a warning sign. Some of those complications can develop rapidly, but most of us can recognize when they are coming on. There are also some drugs that will help prevent some of this from happening. For example, if the heart is beating very rapidly or you feel a pressure in your chest, it can indicate that the blood is not getting to your heart. This can help to prevent damage to it or its vital structures. It is also important that you ask the operating surgeon how he or she feels about the recovery of your patient. Many times the surgeon will indicate the level of concern by his or her tone. Your surgeon is one of many who will be watching your recovery. You should also follow the instructions that are given to you by your surgeon. Any deviation from the protocol can cause problems. Remember, even a tiny change can increase your chance for a poor outcome. Be prepared to ask questions and listen to them carefully. A good surgeon knows what he/she is doing and is confident that his/her plan will work. However, do not be concerned about being negative. After all, you are there to help.

This is a case report and is about a woman who was bitered in the neck by a white widow spider (also called the "Mexican Spider").

So he did some blood tests to find out what was causing the paralysis. One of the tests found that her white blood cells were having an allergic reaction to spider venom. And the reaction was producing cytokines. Cytokines are proteins that help your immune cells fight off infection. This is why the spider was so bad. It was also producing a type B cell antibody which is an antibody that is helpful against infection by white cells. When the white cell antibodies are produced, they can cause you to become paralyzed. Your white bone marrow cells are fighting the infection and are being affected by the antibodies. Because the patient was allergic to venom, the immune systems were overwhelmed and the disease attacked her organs and muscles. Her white body cells became paralyized. She also has to take antibiotics every day for the rest of her life. Also, she has a very serious allergic response to a number of common medications. For example, her blood pressure medication, clonidine, can make her very sleepy. Clonidine is usually used to treat hypertension. That is probably why she needs to have it taken every night. Answer by Dr. David The use of a Biosplenectomy (BS) has become a standard of care for the management of the patient with the diagnosis of liver metastases. While the use for this procedure is not without risk, it is generally considered to be a safe procedure and has been shown to improve survival. The risk for complications with BS is minimal and is usually associated with an increased risk of bleeding. This is a well-recognized risk in the perioperative setting. One of many benefits of BS, in addition to the increased time to complete the procedure, is the ability to accurately determine the number of metastatic lesions. In addition, the BS procedure allows for an evaluation of potential liver remnant volume and the potential for liver resection in select cases. I would suggest that this is one of those situations where a BS may be warranted. Although the risk is clearly present, and although the benefits may outweigh the risks, I do believe that a biopsy of this patient's liver would be indicated. A biopsy may provide information that would help guide management decisions, such as the need to resect liver in this situation. Please see my other response to your question regarding this topic. Best wishes, Dr David

A:Bronchitis is a common condition in the winter months in which you are exposed to damp, cold and dusty environments. A person with bronchitis is likely to cough, have a productive cough (that often comes with a wet, mucousy sputum) and have sore or scratchy throat. Bronchial irritation is an important cause of cough.
Coughing is usually worse when the person is lying down. However, bronchitis can also be caused by colds, viral infections, asthma and lung disorders. In some cases, people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have difficulty with breathing. Asthma is not uncommon in people who have not been exposed, but can occur in those with no known predisposing factors. People with asthma also may have trouble getting enough air in their lungs. Some people can't get enough oxygen to their blood and may be at risk of death. If you have asthma, you should always consult with your doctor to find out whether your condition can be treated. You should not stop taking your medicine without first discussing the treatment with the doctor. For more information on asthma visit the asthma section of our website. It is important that you also discuss your symptoms with doctors who know you well and who can help you to make the right treatment decisions.

If you notice a tear in a baby's gum, this is usually a sign of irritation. A tooth may break in an accident or at night. The tooth might break when the child bites his or her tongue. Some children have a habit of biting their tongues, which may cause a break of the enamel. While it may not be a concern in your case since there are no other signs of tooth decay, a young child may have trouble biting his tongue if his molar is broken.

I am a dermatologist and I have treated a number of patients with similar symptoms.
There are a variety of possible reasons for your symptoms, and no one is better at diagnosing and treating it than a qualified dermatology specialist. The symptoms you describe are most likely an allergic reaction to some type of medication. It is my understanding that some patients take multiple medications to treat multiple symptoms at a time. For example, an allergy to a medication could cause the symptoms on your hands, but your medications may also cause a rash on the legs. This could be one of many possible causes for the rash. If you have not done so already, please review the list of medications you take on this site. text:
Should I seek medical attention?
A:
“Green blood vessels” is not a normal finding. They are a sign of a rare disease called “thromboangiitis obliterans” (T.A.O.)
See this link for more information: 
For your information, "thombo" means "a vein or a blood vessel, especially one that is open or exposed."
The main cause of T. A. O. is a genetic mutation that causes abnormal blood clotting.
T cells have receptors that can recognize these abnormal clots. This is called an immune response. These clumps are called "platelets".
Platelets aggregate in the blood and form a clot. Platelets are formed of the plasma from the bone marrow. Once formed, they travel to the site of injury and stop the bleeding. The clotted blood is then transported to other parts of your body for repair. If the platelets continue to aggregate and travel, the clot can cause damage to nearby tissue, resulting in loss of blood flow. T cells that recognize the platelet aggregates and attack them are the primary cause. 
There are many other causes of this condition, but this is the most common one. Some people may have only one cause, some people have multiple causes. Usually, it's a combination of causes, not one single cause per se. In fact, this can be a result of several different conditions. Your symptoms are an example of one of these conditions, and are not always caused by a single condition. When a person has several possible causes for the same symptoms, doctors can test them all and rule out any single one as the cause and treat the others. Sometimes a patient's symptoms can change and then become worse over time. For example, one person may only have one type of platelet aggregation (a single platelet), but the other person might have several types of aggregation. Other times, a symptom may be present for a long time and only become more severe over the time (for example a condition called fibromuscular dysplasia). It is rare

WHAT SHOULD I DO?
Answer:
This is a typical complication of cellulit and is caused by the accumulation of fluid in the subcutaneous fat tissue around the thighs and buttocks. The most common symptoms are a large swelling of the legs, ankles and feet. In severe cases, swelling can lead to pain and tenderness in an area that is normally warm and cushioned.
The swelling usually subsides after a few days. As the fluid drains out, the swelling will also go down. You should continue to wear compression socks to prevent the skin from pulling and stretching too far. Keep the socks on for at least three days after the treatment and then remove them to allow the wound to heal. Avoid sitting for long periods of time, because that can cause the cellulites to increase. If your cellulite does not go away after two weeks, see your physician for a more detailed examination. Treatment for cellulitic cellulits can be very costly. Your physician may recommend expensive surgical treatments, such as liposuction, or may suggest a combination of both. These treatments are very effective, but they are not always necessary. However, if your doctor recommends them, you should follow his or her directions carefully. It is very important to follow the directions of your health care provider to the letter, no matter how tempting it is to ignore them. Do not hesitate to ask your provider for more information if you have any questions.

A:
According to the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO), the location of the primary tumor is an important prognostic factor. Patients with tumors located on the upper outer quadrant of an ankle joint are considered to have an excellent prognosis. This includes patients with primary breast cancer and patients who have had breast-conserving surgery. In contrast, patients whose tumors are located in the mid or lower outer quadrants of ankles are more likely to experience recurrence and metastasis. These patients are also at a greater risk of developing skeletal-related events. As a result, the ASCO recommends that patients undergoing breast conservation surgery and those who are candidates for breast reconstruction or sentinel lymph node biopsy should have their primary tumors evaluated by a radiation oncologist. When tumors in this location are discovered, they should be treated as early as possible. If tumors cannot be completely removed, radiation therapy or systemic chemotherapy may be used to reduce the risk for recurrence. It is important to note that the treatment plan for these patients will depend upon the type of tumor and the specific location. For patients in whom a tumor was located outside the lower or upper quadrates, surgery is not recommended. However, chemotherapy and radiation are often used in these cases. The treatment plans for patients that have tumors that are not located inside or outside of these regions are discussed in more detail in Section VII of this document.

Any idea what is causing this?
A:
This is usually referred to as a lumbar radiculopathy or sciatica.
It is fairly common and usually related to a number of different things. I'm sure you're not the only one suffering from this. 
An example would be a herniated disc. This can cause the nerve roots to become irritated and cause pain. It can also be caused by a protruding spinal bone, which can lead to nerve irritation. Another example is nerve root irritation caused from the muscles in your lower back. Muscles can sometimes cause irritation and pain to your nerve. They also can tear in muscles that are weak and become spasm (like a muscle that can't properly relax and relax).
Your muscles can tighten in response to pain and tightness in a back that has been injured. Injuries can often cause your muscles to tight up, and if you don't get the pain under control, it can result in further injury. Pain is not usually an indicator of injury, so if your pain is getting worse, you might want to get checked out. If you are experiencing pain that gets worse with activity, talk to someone about it. Maybe you should get a new job. Or maybe you need to move to the right spot. You could also try a physical therapist for a pain management program. Physical therapy might be able to help with pain or muscle tightening. There is a very good chance that you have a nerve issue that needs to be addressed. 
You might also have some nerve compression or irritation in one of the lower thoracic (chest) vertebrae. A thoracic vertebra is one just behind your heart. When there is irritation or compression, your nerves can get pinched or compressed in that area. The pain can be excruciating and can make it hard for you to breathe. Sometimes you can feel a sharp pain where the spinal cord (nerve) is compressed. But this only happens with nerve irritations. Usually the thoracic nerve is just irritated.

There are different treatment options depending on what is causing the damage. For example, if you are experiencing hair shedding due to stress and you believe that the condition is due a fungal infection, there are antifungal creams that are effective. However, it would likely be necessary to order a thorough exam to determine what's causing your problem. @Reply to comment Yes, please see your doctor. You may need stitches. If there is no scarring, it is unlikely to develop into a larger wound, but the dog will be bitten again, and if there are any problems, you will need a second opinion. Don't let your dog do any activity where it might hurt you. Your dog is a protector of you, so protect it. Make sure it has plenty of exercise and walks. A good food diet will make sure that your pet is healthy. Good luck.

Doctor Answers (6)
1 by Anonymous from United States This may be a sign of infection, especially if it is a mild infection.
I would recommend that you have a pelvic exam, a vaginal exam and a rectal exam. Also, you may have bacterial vaginosis, so you will need to have some kind of culture done. I would also recommend a new yeast infection test if you are having vaginal discharge. These tests can be done on an outpatient basis. Antibiotics are not usually prescribed for vaginal infections. If you do need antibiotics, the drugs you should use are the ones that work for the most common bacterial infections, such as the flu. You may also want to see your gynecologist. Good luck!
